turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity pulling on Earth’s oceans, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, different places move through these areas of higher and lower water levels, creating high and low tides. The shape of coastlines and ocean depths influence how strong tides are in different locations. Most coastal areas experience two high tides and two low tides each day, though timing and height vary depending on local conditions and the positions of the Moon and Sun.
